units.text: INT. GHOSTS - CONTINUOUS
Well, it may be so.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: He feels so acutely that he needs some one to keep a firm hold on him when temptation comes. That is what I cannot help liking about Jacob Engstrand: he comes to you so helplessly, accusing himself and confessing his own weakness. The last time he was talking to me--Believe me, Mrs. Alving, supposing it were a real necessity for him to have Regina home again--
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Rising hastily.
Regina!
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: --you must not set yourself against it.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Indeed I shall set myself against it. And besides--Regina is to have a position in the Orphanage.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: But, after all, remember he is her father--
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Oh, I know very well what sort of a father he has been to her. No! She shall never go to him with my goodwill.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Rising.
My dear lady, don't take the matter so warmly. You sadly misjudge poor Engstrand. You seem to be quite terrified--
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: More quietly.
It makes no difference. I have taken Regina into my house, and there she shall stay.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Listens.
Hush, my dear Mr. Manders; say no more about it.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Her face lights up with gladness.
Listen! there is Oswald coming downstairs. Now we'll think of no one but him.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: OSWALD ALVING, in a light overcoat, hat in hand, and smoking a large meerschaum, enters by the door on the left; he stops in the doorway.
Oh, I beg your pardon; I thought you were in the study.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Comes forward.
Good-morning, Pastor Manders.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Staring.
Ah--! How strange--!
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Well now, what do you think of him, Mr. Manders?
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: I--I--can it really be--?
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Yes, it's really the Prodigal Son, sir.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Protesting.
My dear young friend--
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Well, then, the Lost Sheep Found.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Oswald is thinking of the time when you were so much opposed to his becoming a painter.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: To our human eyes many a step seems dubious, which afterwards proves--
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Wrings his hand.
But first of all, welcome, welcome home! Do not think, my dear Oswald--I suppose I may call you by your Christian name?
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: What else should you call me?
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Very good. What I wanted to say was this, my dear Oswald you must not think that I utterly condemn the artist's calling. I have no doubt there are many who can keep their inner self unharmed in that profession, as in any other.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Let us hope so.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Beaming with delight.
I know one who has kept both his inner and his outer self unharmed. Just look at him, Mr. Manders.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: Moves restlessly about the room.
Yes, yes, my dear mother; let's say no more about it.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Why, certainly--that is undeniable. And you have begun to make a name for yourself already. The newspapers have often spoken of you, most favourably. Just lately, by-the-bye, I fancy I haven't seen your name quite so often.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Up in the conservatory.
I haven't been able to paint so much lately.
units.name: OSWALD

units.text: Even a painter needs a little rest now and then.
units.name: MRS. ALVING

units.text: No doubt, no doubt. And meanwhile he can be preparing himself and mustering his forces for some great work.
units.name: MANDERS

units.text: Yes.--Mother, will dinner soon be ready?
units.name: OSWALD
